prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it answers this question: how many app sessions did the users of each account have in November 2025? Use only the app events from 1 to 30 November 2025 (UTC days of event_ts), so a user's first event in November starts a session. A user's first app event starts a session, and an event more than 30 minutes after the same user's previous event starts a new one; an event exactly 30 minutes later stays in the same session. Measure each gap as the time between the two moments in event_ts, a UTC instant, never between clock times. Return two columns, in this order: account_id and sessions. Return one row for each account with app events in November. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, check how the gap is measured: date_diff with 'minute' counts minute boundaries, not minutes.
From 09:06:50 to 09:36:51 is more than 30 minutes, yet only 30 minute boundaries are crossed; compare the gap itself instead.
starter_sql:
WITH gaps AS (
  -- one row per app event in November 2025
  SELECT user_id, account_id, event_ts,
    LAG(event_ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY event_ts, event_id) AS prev_ts
  FROM app_events
  WHERE event_ts >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-11-01 00:00:00+00'
    AND event_ts < TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-12-01 00:00:00+00'
), flagged AS (
  -- one row per app event in November 2025
  SELECT user_id, account_id, event_ts,
    CASE WHEN prev_ts IS NULL OR date_diff('minute', prev_ts, event_ts) > 30 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS new_session
  FROM gaps
)
SELECT account_id, SUM(new_session) AS sessions
FROM flagged
GROUP BY account_id
why_this_works: Comparing the interval between the two moments with 30 minutes measures the real gap, so 30 minutes and 1 second opens a session.
